completion_conditions: All three sites resolve the default branch from origin, and a stale local ref no longer changes the diff the reviewer receives.
A regression test fails if any of the three reverts to a bare local name.
The full suite, the goal-loop suite, the module-boundaries suite and validate_shiki stay green.

decisions: Three sites in `scripts/shiki_loop.py` resolve the default branch by a BARE LOCAL NAME, verified on origin/main: line 802 `git rev-list --count main..HEAD` (the ahead-count that decides whether an implementation was pushed), line 1039 `git diff --cached main` (the diff handed to the pre-PR reviewer), and line 1042 `git diff main...HEAD` (its fallback).

Measured harm 2026-08-03: the coordinator's local `main` was 151 commits behind `origin/main`. `git diff --cached main` produced 2,904,002 bytes across 697 files; the same diff against `origin/main` was 47,899 bytes across 4 files — a 47x difference on bytes. The reviewer process exited 1, and `_run_pre_pr_code_review` fails closed to `stop_blocked` with 'no PR exists to anchor a repair', which is terminal: there is no repair path and no retry. Fast-forwarding the local ref by hand was the only recovery.

This is a RECURRENCE, not a new class. The same defect was fixed once in `scripts/shiki_runtime.py`, where `resolve_default_branch_ref` (line 332) already fetches and prefers `origin/<name>`. `scripts/shiki_loop.py` line 30 already imports from `shiki_runtime`, so the correct resolution is one import away and was simply not applied here.

LOCK-SUFFICIENCY CHECK (2026-08-05). MUST-CHANGE: `scripts/shiki_loop.py` (the three sites plus the stale comment at :1036 and the prompt string at :1001 that both name a bare `main`); `tests/test_loop_code_review.py` — the existing driver of `_run_pre_pr_code_review`, which must gain a stale-local-`main` regression; `tests/test_repair_delivery.py` — its harness helper mirrors the :802 ahead-count and would drift.

DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: `scripts/shiki_runtime.py` — `resolve_default_branch_ref` is already correct and importing it unchanged breaks nothing. Lock it only if the function has to move, which this task does not require.

MUST-NOT-BREAK (verification command, not locks): `tests/test_loop_tdd_evidence.py` monkeypatches `_run_pre_pr_code_review` with the signature `(target, task_id)`, so that signature must not change; `tests/test_worktree_base.py` pins the runtime helper's behaviour; `scripts/test_shiki_module_boundaries.sh` pins the import graph; `scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh` drives the loop end to end.

OUT OF SCOPE, recorded not fixed: a lower-severity sibling class exists where the literal `"main"` is used but already in the correct `origin/` form — `shiki_loop.py` lines 1271, 1273, 1336, 1398, 1436, 1453, 1545, 1554, 1565, 1728 and `scripts/shiki.py:24`, `scripts/shiki_cli.py:39,163,322`. Widening the scope to a repository-wide default-branch abstraction would pull in five more files and collide with four other backlog items; it is a separate decision.

Risk is medium and honest: this changes how the loop resolves a git ref, not what any gate enforces. No approval source, schema, workflow or MergeGate rule moves. Under `.shiki/guardian-policy.json` (`applies_to_risk: [high, critical]`) neither the Contract PR nor the implementation PR triggers the Guardian gate, so this goal costs zero operator approvals.
grill_with_docs.source: Measured 2026-08-03 during a live dispatch; sites re-verified against origin/main 2026-08-05.

non_goals: Introducing a repository-wide default-branch abstraction, or touching the sibling sites that already use the correct origin/ form.
Changing what the pre-PR reviewer judges, or any gate, schema or workflow.
Adding a retry to the pre-PR reviewer — that is a separate decision.
Touching any file outside the declared locks.
outcome: The goal loop's pre-PR reviewer and its ahead-count read the default branch from `origin/<default>` rather than a bare local `main`, so a coordinator whose local ref has fallen behind no longer feeds the reviewer an enormous unrelated diff. Measured: a local `main` 151 commits behind produced a 2.9 MB / 697-file diff where the real change was 4 files / 48 KB, and the reviewer process exited 1 — a terminal `stop_blocked` with no recourse.

spec_freeze.source: Operator instruction 2026-08-05 to work the remaining backlog in the audited recommended order; G is first because it is the only item with zero lock conflicts against every other item and it has measured, reproducible harm.

acceptance_checks: All three sites (the ahead-count, the reviewer diff and its fallback) resolve the default branch from origin via resolve_default_branch_ref, imported from shiki_runtime and not reimplemented.
The comment at the reviewer-diff site and the reviewer prompt string no longer name a bare local branch.
A fetch failure degrades to today's behaviour and never crashes the loop.

A regression in tests/test_loop_code_review.py builds a real repository whose local default ref lags its remote and asserts the reviewer's diff contains only the task's own change — asserted by file count or byte size, not by content sampling.
The regression FAILS if a site is reverted to a bare local name — proved by the test, not only by passing today.
tests/test_repair_delivery.py's harness helper matches the line-802 resolution so the two cannot drift.
_run_pre_pr_code_review keeps the (target, task_id) signature that tests/test_loop_tdd_evidence.py monkeypatches.
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests, scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh, scripts/test_shiki_module_boundaries.sh and validate_shiki all pass.
No file outside the declared locks is changed.

Adding a retry to the pre-PR reviewer
Changing what the reviewer judges, or any gate/schema/workflow

tasks.scope:
In `scripts/shiki_loop.py`, replace the bare local default-branch name at all three sites with a ref resolved from origin, reusing `resolve_default_branch_ref` from `scripts/shiki_runtime.py` (already imported at line 30 — import the function, do not copy its logic, and do not modify `shiki_runtime.py`):
  - line 802 `git rev-list --count main..HEAD` — the ahead-count that decides whether an implementation reached the task branch;
  - line 1039 `git diff --cached main` — the diff handed to the pre-PR reviewer;
  - line 1042 `git diff main...HEAD` — its fallback.
Also correct the stale comment at line 1036 and the prompt string at line 1001, both of which name a bare `main`.

The resolution must be the SAME one `shiki_runtime` already performs: best-effort `git fetch origin <name>`, then prefer `origin/<name>` and fall back to the bare name only when the remote-tracking ref cannot be resolved. A fetch failure must not crash the loop — it degrades to today's behaviour.

Do NOT change the signature of `_run_pre_pr_code_review`: `tests/test_loop_tdd_evidence.py` monkeypatches it as `(target, task_id)`.

Add a regression to `tests/test_loop_code_review.py` modelled on `tests/test_worktree_base.py`'s `test_cuts_from_remote_tip_when_local_default_lags`: build a real temporary repository whose local default ref LAGS its remote-tracking ref, drive `_run_pre_pr_code_review`, and assert the diff the reviewer receives contains only the task's own change — not the commits the local ref is missing. Assert the byte size or file count directly, so a regression is loud rather than a subtle content difference. Update `tests/test_repair_delivery.py`'s harness helper, which mirrors the line-802 ahead-count, so the two cannot drift.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: `shiki loop` reports `pre-PR code review did not pass (reviewer exited 1; failing closed); no PR exists to anchor a repair — diagnose or re-dispatch`. The implementation is correct and the reviewer never judged it: it was handed a diff of the entire repository's recent history. The stop is terminal — there is no repair path, no retry, and no PR to anchor one.
  Measured 2026-08-03 on a live dispatch: local `main` 151 commits behind `origin/main`. `git diff --cached main` -> 2,904,002 bytes / 697 files. `git diff --cached origin/main` -> 47,899 bytes / 4 files. Fast-forwarding the local ref by hand made the same task pass on the next attempt with no code change.
  Root cause: three sites resolve the default branch by a bare local name. Nothing keeps a coordinator's local `main` current — the loop fetches `origin/main` for its own merges but never updates the local ref, so the gap grows silently with every merge.
  Why it is a recurrence: `scripts/shiki_runtime.py:332` `resolve_default_branch_ref` already fetches and prefers `origin/<name>`; that fix was applied there and not here, and `shiki_loop.py:30` already imports from that module.
  Reproducible when: a repository whose local default ref lags its remote produces a reviewer diff containing only the task's own change, and a regression test fails if any site reverts to a bare local name.
